pamphlet_excerpts: Fingers Probably Useful: Fingers probably are the most useful tools for working with softclays.
Loop Tool Wooden: You can use a loop tool, a wooden tool with a metal loopon the end, to trim away excess clay.
Working Withsoapstone Soft: If you are working withsoapstone (a soft stone), you will need a rasp and a riffler, ametal tool similar to a rasp with fine, small cutting points.
Commercial Tools Come: These commercial tools come in handyfor the artist working with clay.
step_by_step_procedure: Wood-carving Tools Asrasps: Use wood-carving tools, such asrasps, files, gouges, chisels, and V-tools, with great care.
Soapstone Quite Soft: Even though soapstone is quite soft, it still requires a lotof effort to carve a form.
Whenever Yousee Icon: Whenever yousee this icon, there will besafety informationthat goes with it.
Knives Andchisels Wood: When using knives andchisels to make wood sculptures, always carve and cut awayfrom your body.

requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following: (a) Model in clay a life-size human head. Then sculpt in modeling clay, carve in wood or plaster, or use 3D modeling software to make a small-scale model of an animal or person. Explain to your counselor the method and tools you used to sculpt the figure. (b) Make a plaster mold of a fruit or vegetable. In this mold, make a copy of the fruit or vegetable. Explain to your counselor the method and tools you used to make the copy. (c) With your parent or guardian's permission and your counselor's approval, visit a museum, art exhibit, art gallery, artists' co-op, or artist's studio. After your visit, share with your counselor what you have learned. Discuss the importance of visual arts and how it strengthens social tolerance and helps stimulate cultural, intellectual, and personal development.

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to this merit badge. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. Your research methods may include—with your parent or guardian's permission—an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career. Resources: 12 Careers for Sculptors (website) How To Become an Artist/Sculptor (video) Craft Artist Careers (video) (b) Explore how you could use knowledge and skills from this merit badge to pursue a hobby. Research any training needed, expenses, and organizations that promote or support it. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.

pamphlet_excerpts: Want Pursue Career: If you want to pursue a career as aprofessional sculptor, you will needsome studio lessons and hands-ontraining.
Start Findingout High: You can start by findingout if your high school offers shopclasses that will introduce you tothe techniques for working withmetal, wood, and plastics.
Later Hands-on Training: Later, you can get hands-on training byworking for another artist as anapprentice or assistant.
Youintend Supplement: If youintend to supplement your incomein a related field, you might have toearn advanced degrees.
step_by_step_procedure: Colleges Universities: Colleges and universities offerfour- and five-year programs thatlead to bachelor of fine arts (BFA) or master of fine arts (MFA) degrees.
Beyond Core Coursescommon: Beyond the core coursescommon to all major areas ofstudy, these programs include art history and studio art classes.
Independent Schools Art: Independent schools of art and design offer two-yearprograms that lead to an associate of arts or bachelor of finearts degree.
Anyone Wants Teach: Anyone who wants to teach art in public schools must have a bachelor’s degree; you might also need a teaching certificate.
